task: ch14 ordinary-control manual walk freeze at steps[38]
verdict: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED: terrain/collision. The body left the supported walk surface at a measured support gap (submerged shoreline ledge) on the ch14-scar approach, fell 0.326u below the floor plane, and became geometrically wedged: horizontal resolution returned a bit-identical position and gravity was already floor-clamped. Not survival/downed, not input/focus, not a render/physics stall, not a controller error.

sourceParity.driftNature: npm script definitions only; no game source, no bundled asset. Served bundle hash-verified identical to the failing run.

reproduction.inference: The defect is intermittent and timing-dependent, not deterministic. A single passing replay cannot certify the fix and does not clear the blocker.

causalChain: 1. A real support gap exists on the ch14-scar walk route. In the passing replay, /commonGround/supported reads FALSE at bodyPose [-41.876,50.977,10.824] and [-41.233,50.896,10.471]; the same band was hit earlier at bootstrap[36] ([-41.637,50.990,11.413], [-42.449,50.990,11.413]). Band approx x in [-42.45,-41.23], z in [10.47,11.41], floor plane y ~= 50.99.

2. Crossing the gap, support is lost and the body falls. In the passing run the fall was shallow (y 50.989 -> 50.896, -0.093) and forward momentum carried the body across within 2 samples; y then recovered to 51.223 and the walk continued.
3. In the failing run the body entered the same band and fell deeper: y 50.989 -> 50.723 -> 50.663 (-0.326) at [-41.446,50.663,10.521], which lies inside the measured unsupported band.

4. At that depth the body is below the surrounding floor lip and is pinned. Vertical motion is floor-clamped (y stops exactly and never decays further, so it is resting on collision, not free-falling). Horizontal motion resolves to the identical clamped value every tick, so bodyPose is BIT-IDENTICAL for 7.48s across 37 consecutive samples.

5. The walk driver cannot recover from a total wedge. In walkByInputs (main/tools/chapter-loop/control-capture.mjs), disagreements only increments when moved > 0.02; a full wedge has moved ~= 0, which RESETS disagreements to 0. Recalibration and direction change therefore never fire. The driver holds the same W+D chord for the full noProgressMs (8000ms) and throws "Walk stopped making progress toward its target".

survivalOrDowned.evidence: Failure frame raw/frame-5.png shows SUIT HUD HEALTH 100%, FOOD 89%, WATER 84%, TEMP 100%, STAM 100%, OXY 100%. isDowned() is health<=0 (main/src/game/systems/survivalVitals.ts:111) and no downed gate exists in commonGroundDirector or the surface-motion path. Story remained active and unpaused with unchanged objective feedback.

inputOrFocus.evidence: The same held W+D chord drove the body ~2.9u at ~4.7u/s in the 1.2s immediately before the freeze. input.hotkeyActivations reached 212 with revision 212 and targetEditable false on every event. Absence of new input events during the freeze is expected: heldWalkInput keeps keys down and emits no repeat up/down.

renderOrPhysicsStall.evidence: The probe bridge executed page.evaluate on the page main thread every ~200ms for the full 8s with runtimeReady true, so the JS main thread was never blocked. The body also came to rest at a floor-clamped value rather than freezing mid-descent, which requires the physics step to have run and clamped it.

controllerError.evidence: No pageerrors in the failing run and none in this replay (observations.json pageErrors empty). /commonGround/diagnostic/holdReason was null throughout the freeze and /commonGround/worldBound stayed true.

diagnosticMethod.injections: none: no state injection, teleport, progress setter or debug script

notes: The failing run and this replay are the same immutable build; the failure is not a stale-candidate artifact.
This diagnostic duplicate is noncertifying: it passed, so it proves the path CAN complete, not that the defect is gone.

Two independent contributors are in evidence: a world-geometry support gap (game source) and a walk-driver wedge-recovery blind spot (harness tool). Fixing only the harness would hide the gap; fixing only the gap leaves the driver unable to report future wedges.
